name: Warlord Dorinakka

facts.text: Level 81, 100,000 health, tether 2,000. Pulling him brings twelve crypt knights.
The bounty quest's hunt reason says he rallies Caer Sidi's war-dead.

story:
Dorinakka was sent to Caer Sidi because he would not lay down his sword, and he has not laid it down yet. He commanded a warband in a war nobody remembers and died at its head, and when Arawn's keepers came for him he fought them too. When the gaol rose he took the yard and found Arawn's own crypt knights there, and he did what he had always done: he drilled them. Twelve of them march at his back now, and they come when he calls.

Who he was. Dorinakka commanded a warband in a war nobody now remembers, on a shore nobody now names, and he died at its head with his sword in his hand. When Arawn's keepers came for his soul he fought them too, and killed two, and so he was sent not to the Deadlands but to Caer Sidi, with the others who would not lay down their swords.

The yard. He has not laid it down yet. When the gaol rose he took the yard where Arawn's crypt knights drilled, and found the knights still there, leaderless, and he did what he had always done: he drilled them. Twelve of them march at his back now, in better order than they ever kept for Arawn, and they come when he calls. Before every drill he salutes toward the hall above where Bellum rides, because the warlord knows his own god when he sees him. The bounty-masters of Albion say he rallies Caer Sidi's war-dead; the Inconnu say the Crypt Lord gives him orders, and that Dorinakka has not yet noticed.
legend: Twelve crypt knights come with him. Keep him inside his short tether, about two thousand units; drag him further and he walks home. Off-tanks pick up the knights and kill them while the main tank holds the warlord, and the casters stand where the knights cannot reach them. A straight brawl, but a big one, and the knights hit hard. The knights are the fight. If you have the off-tanks, kill them in pairs from the end of the line inward, and the warlord comes apart without them. If you do not have the off-tanks, do not pull the yard.

aggro: Form ranks! The living are at the gate!
I did not lay it down for Arawn. I will not for you.

loremasterTopic.text: A warlord who would not lay down his sword, alive or dead. He took the yard of Caer Sidi and drills Arawn's own crypt knights. Twelve of them march at his back.

bookPage: In the yard the dead knights were at drill when we came, twelve of them in a line, and their warlord walking the line as a living sergeant would, correcting the angle of a shield here, the set of a foot there. He saw us and did not hurry. He formed them up. He told them the living were at the gate. Then he came at us at their head, and it was the best-ordered charge I have ever faced. Brother Cadoc said afterwards that it was almost a pity to break it. I did not think it was a pity at all.
